moved.sentence: **Protocol/interface + implementors form one unit.** If a file defines a protocol and a second file is its primary concrete implementation, they belong in the same scope group unless the implementation is independently large enough to warrant separation (50+ files).

judged.note: should-group-protocol-with-primary-implementation keeps the protocol-plus-primary-implementation same-group call, its 50+-files exception and the one-unit headline.

moved.sentence: **Barrel files define the interface boundary.** Everything a barrel re-exports is part of the same public surface.

judged.note: should-treat-barrel-reexports-as-one-candidate keeps 'barrel files define the interface boundary' and the rationale keeps that everything a barrel re-exports is one public surface.

moved.sentence: If the barrel re-exports from five subdirectories, those subdirectories share an interface and are candidates for a single scope group — unless they are large enough to warrant separate groups that share a common API layer.

judged.note: should-treat-barrel-reexports-as-one-candidate keeps the five-subdirectory case, the shared interface, single-group candidacy and the large-enough-for-separate-groups-with-shared-API exception.

moved.sentence: **Shared types follow their primary consumer, not their definition file.** A `UserProfile` struct defined in `Models/` but used only by the `Auth` module belongs in the `Auth` scope group.

judged.note: should-place-shared-types-with-primary-consumer keeps the primary-consumer placement and the UserProfile-in-Models-used-only-by-Auth example.

moved.sentence: **Fragmented interfaces are a smell.** If the same logical interface is declared across three files with no organizing barrel, note this as a cohesion anomaly — it indicates the public surface has not been intentionally designed.

judged.note: should-note-fragmented-interfaces keeps the three-files-no-barrel condition and noting it as a cohesion anomaly; the rationale keeps the not-intentionally-designed reason.

moved.sentence: **Internal helpers are not interface.** Private/internal/file-private symbols do not contribute to interface cohesion; they contribute to implementation cohesion analyzed by `dependency-clusters`.

judged.note: should-not-count-internal-helpers-as-interface keeps private/internal/file-private symbols out of interface cohesion and their role in implementation cohesion under dependency-clusters.
